name: Kopi powder
description: Coffee beans, mostly robusta, roasted dark with a little sugar and margarine and ground fine. Bold, smoky and slightly caramel.
caffeineSource: Robusta coffee is about 2.2% caffeine by weight (International Coffee Organization; Farah, Coffee Constituents, 2012). Allowing for the roasting sugar and about 80% extraction through a sock gives roughly 15 mg per gram.

name: Tea dust
description: Finely broken black tea leaves that brew strong, dark and slightly bitter in a few minutes.
caffeineSource: Black tea leaves are about 2.5–3.5% caffeine by weight (Hicks, McCaig and Fraser, Journal of Food Science, 1996). A strong brew draws out most of it: roughly 18 mg per gram.

name: Condensed milk
description: Milk cooked down with sugar until thick and sweet. One spoonful whitens and sweetens a cup at once.

name: Evaporated milk
description: Milk cooked down without sugar. Creamy and a little toasty, it whitens a drink without sweetening it.

name: Sugar
description: Plain white sugar. It dissolves fastest while the drink is hot.

name: Boiling water
description: Water just off the boil, for brewing.

name: Water
description: Plain water to lengthen the drink: hot for a hot drink, cold for an iced one.

name: Ice
description: Ice cubes.

name: Milo powder
description: A malted chocolate drink powder made from barley malt, milk powder and cocoa.
caffeineSource: Cocoa powder has about 230 mg of caffeine per 100 g (USDA FoodData Central). Milo is only partly cocoa, giving an estimated 2 mg per tablespoon. To be checked against the tin.

name: Horlicks powder
description: A malted milk drink powder made from wheat, barley malt and milk. Sweet, biscuity and caffeine-free.

name: Pearl barley
description: Polished barley grains that turn soft as they cook and give their water a gentle, nutty taste.

name: Dried chrysanthemum flowers
description: Small dried yellow flowers that brew a golden, floral, faintly honeyed tea with no caffeine.

name: Water chestnuts
description: Crisp, sweet corms with a dark skin. Fresh ones need peeling; tinned ones are ready to use.

name: Calamansi
description: Small, round green limes with a fragrant, tangy juice. Ordinary limes can stand in.

name: Rose syrup
description: A bright pink, very sweet syrup with the scent of roses. Check that the label lists only sugar, water, rose flavouring and colouring.

name: Ginger
description: Fresh ginger root. Warm and peppery, it gives a drink a gentle heat.

name: Unsweetened soy milk
description: Plain soy milk with nothing added, from a carton or a soya bean stall.

name: Pandan leaf
description: A long green leaf with a sweet, grassy, vanilla-like scent, tied in a knot to flavour drinks.

name: Espresso
description: A small, strong shot of coffee pressed through finely ground beans.

name: Milk
description: Fresh full-cream milk. It steams and froths best cold from the fridge.
